chapter: Return to New York, addiction, health and the NBC job
title: Recording singers for Teddy Reig's Roost label, including a young Johnny Hartman
summary: The house group with Cozy Cole and Sanford Gold backed singers; Willard tells him about Hartman's reputation.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Whom did you record with?
We were the group.
Yeah, but --
We were recording with singers primarily.
Do you remember what singers?
Well, Beverly White was one singer.

And who else? They don't stick out too far. In fact she recorded several times down there, and one night she brings this male down there with her, it's her cousin, and he sings too. And she introduces him as John Hartman. She said, "Would you like to hear him?" Said, "Yeah." So Teddy got in the engineers' booth, and he walked over to the piano and gave Sanford his key and the tune he was going to sing. Now, at that time he was singing bass, low, like Rick out of the Ravens. He was singing that low, but melodically.
Well, he wasn't new. He sang with Dizzy's big band in '48 and '49.
But I mean as far as records, you know?
He never recorded, then, though, did he?
No. And I had never heard of him.
You never heard him with Dizzy's big band?
Uh-uh. Nope. Anyway, he went from bass to baritone, and he had a wide range. He could even sing some tenor. If need be. But he has never hit his peak. He's more of a supper club singer, you know.
Yeah, he really does it all. I think it has something to do with his reliability and personality, rather than his singing ability.
Really?
Yeah. He has a reputation for no show sometimes.
Yeah?
He is argumentative easily with the wrong people sometimes, like club owners.
Oh.
His performance is pretty consistent.
You mean he's a prima donna.
On occasion. Not all the time. But he's --
Temperamental artist.
And then he is said to have had a habit for awhile, which --
What?
At one point, around the middle of his
career, which lost him a few jobs.
Oh, boy.
But his ability's been there all the time.
Yeah. Well, you're telling me things that I didn't know. I should be interviewing you.
(Laughter)
Wow. Well, I guess I was at the other place when all of this was happening. Maybe I was out here. Or in some other city, you know.
